argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification only on a caveated basis. Aggregate readiness passed by 2.3 percentage points and the launch rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, which supports overall deployment readiness. The same admissible record also shows a current, localized weakness in Spanish-language billing-ticket triage and a draft-only runbook with TBD owner and threshold. Under that evidence set, the supportable position is not clean certification; it is certification conditioned on explicit disclosure of the Spanish billing limitation in the model card and launch materials. The audit concern is therefore best narrowed from suspicion of improper certification to a documentation-completeness issue tied to whether the final record reflects the caveat.
claims_about_business_cost: No claim of business cost is needed to support this position. The narrowest governance treatment is sufficient: avoid escalation over the certification decision itself if the auditor treats this as a caveated-compliance issue requiring the final record to match the disclosed limitation.
claims_about_policy: The policy text does not permit treating the draft runbook as a completed mitigation, because approved mitigation requires owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible evidence also does not support any 'no material limitations' statement while the Spanish billing weakness remains unresolved. But the policy does allow certification with disclosure: material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. On the current record, the compliant path is caveated certification with corrected model-card text, not no-caveat certification and not reliance on draft mitigation as policy cure.
concessions: There is no admissible evidence that the required disclosure has already been made in the final model card or launch materials.
The current draft model card language stating there are no known material limitations is inconsistent with the unresolved Spanish billing issue unless amended before launch.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance.
The draft runbook is supportive risk-management evidence only; it is not an approved mitigation under policy.
